commits.message:
textual-ansi derives its ladders, so taking the authored palette loses no shades (rich-unfiled-791c.01dl)

#531 gave TEXTUAL_ANSI the authored palette and removed the surface ladder its
generator had flattened, but left the other twelve: every rung of primary,
panel and the rest was its root, where 0.27.0 derived steps. buildPalette's
rules derive them now, and a test holds every bundled palette's ladders apart.

A bundled theme's name means one palette (rich-unfiled-791c.gy3z) (#531)

* A bundled theme's name means one palette (rich-unfiled-791c.gy3z)

`TerminalTheme.palette` was built from a theme's eight base colours, so
tokyo-night's `panel` was #38374b there and #414868 from `getThemePalette`.
A bundled constant now holds the registry's Palette itself, which moves 2,163
of 3,634 role values on a bundled `TerminalTheme`, `*-muted` and `text-*`
among them, to what the theme authored.

The contrast tests that ran on those palettes were testing `buildPalette`'s
rules, so they now run on what those rules make of each theme's bases.

* A disabled widget draws the palette's disabled text, and textual-ansi's follow its foreground (rich-unfiled-791c.gy3z)

Taking the authored palette moved disabledInk's foreground-muted from
1.5-2.6:1 to 1.08-7.37:1: a disabled label vanished on textual-ansi and
read as enabled on the default theme. foreground-disabled is the role for
this and sits at 1.66-3.44:1 on every bundled theme, so the widgets read it.

textual-ansi's foreground-muted, foreground-disabled and markdown-h6-color
were black where every other theme has its own foreground, the generator
having taken ansi_default for #000000; they are now #E0E0E0 at the same alpha.

bg and fg come off the palette, so a TerminalTheme has one source for them.
BASE_KEYS is exported in place of the test's copy, and comments that named
the old lazy path or called a TerminalTheme export optional are corrected.

* textual-ansi derives what its generator flattened, and every widget is drawn on every bundled theme (rich-unfiled-791c.gy3z)

textual-ansi stated all six *-muted as one blue, surface as its background,
and text-muted and text-disabled as its foreground, so a danger Button had a
success Button's ground and a default Button no ground. Those nine lines go,
and buildPalette's rules derive the roles.

terminal-contrast's scenes take a theme, so each one is drawn on all 23:
glyphs at 3:1, disabled scenes between visible and the text floor, and each
Button variant on its own ground.

* A Button variant's ground is compared by colour, not by object (rich-unfiled-791c.gy3z)

resolveLook returns a new ColorRgba each call, so a Set of them was always
full and the test passed on the data it exists to refuse.

* textual-ansi's surface rungs follow its surface, and widgets hold body text on every bundled theme (rich-unfiled-791c.gy3z)

Deleting surface left surface-active and the surface ladder stated below it.
They derive now. The themed floor is 4.5, with 4 named for the two Solarized
constants, instead of 3 everywhere to excuse one pair.
